angles.drive: Looking after what you have is the work you trust. Wood runs plentiful in you, so something is always growing under your hands and the growing rewards whoever stays. You tend the same few things until they pay, or you keep them because leaving is harder. The price is the doors you never tried.

angles.cost_self: Putting something aside before you enjoy anything is automatic for you. Wood grows thick in you, and there is always something worth keeping. You save because the future is real to you, or because spending feels like losing. It costs you every small comfort you could afford and never take. Rest is one of them.

angles.drive: Improving what you already own comes easier to you than chasing what you don’t, and it shows everywhere you’ve settled. Care, in your hands, behaves like an investment: whatever you maintain appreciates, and whatever needs chasing, you mostly no longer bother to chase.

angles.cost_self: Fifty a month since college. A page a day, a call every Friday, and at no point did any of it look impressive, which is exactly why it worked. Your natural size of effort is small enough to repeat forever, and repetition is where your money and your skill actually come from.

ledger: the Steward's value built and kept: staying that pays, priced in doors untried
the Steward's thrift: saving before enjoying, priced in comfort and rest not taken
